diffs.diff: header pin 1: part says SPEED, datasheet reading says Wire 1
diffs.evidence: Naming difference only: the product is a passive, unpolarised 2-wire reed switch (Sheldon Brown: 'If the circuit is still open, the wire, or reed switch, is bad'), so its two unlabelled wires (the second reading's Wire 1 / Wire 2) are interchangeable; the model names the one that goes to the GPIO with pull-up SPEED, matching the standard wiring where the sensor uses 'GND and digital pin 2 and uses the board' internal pull-up.

diffs.diff: header pin 2: part says GND, datasheet reading says Wire 2
diffs.evidence: Naming difference only: the reed switch has two interchangeable, unpolarised wires, and the model assigns the second wire to ground as in the standard wiring where 'The sensor is connected to the Arduino' GND and a GPIO with pull-up; the switch simply shorts this wire to the pin, so either wire may be GND (Sheldon Brown: 'If the circuit is still open, the wire, or reed switch, is bad').
